svg.title: Concert Pricing Desk Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-concert-pricing-desk-architecture; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Concert Pricing Desk Architecture; subtitle: Four controls around the gap between face value and market price; caption: How a concert buying operation organizes around presale timing, checkout verification, fee drag and face-value caps.; assumptions note: Headcount was not stated by any practitioner; the structure maps to operator gates, not a staffing plan.; note: Sources: thumbsuprun (TpXJCfuFf4o @ 00:06:35), Scott Cramer (kFsH01UthzA @ 00:11:23 and 00:23:58), Why It Costs (tH7bLaJI6ZE @ 00:08:16), Business Made Simple (VBp4zpS7F3o @ 00:09:17).; center: role: Concert Pricing Desk; headcount: Not stated by practitioners; focus: Run every deal on the all-in number: add every line, divide by face value, and compare totals across sites.; spokes: role: Presale Entry; type: Access; kpi: First presale wave entered before Official Platinum conversion or face-value increases.; role: Checkout Price Verification; type: Control; kpi: Final payment screen re-checked; a Shania Twain order at $227 each became $291 apiece, a 30% bump.; role: Fee-Drag Underwriting; type: Risk; kpi: Secondary fees averaged 31% of listed price in the GAO sample; weak demand can leave resale losses.; role: Face-Value Cap Screening; type: Compliance; kpi: Tours like Noah Kahan's allow resale only on Ticketmaster at base price, so the markup disappears.
